antusuchus:table:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (table of new taxa)

antusuchus:study:1.title: A new early peirosaurid terrestrial crocodile (Notosuchia) from La Buitrera (Candeleros Formation), Río Negro, Argentina (Historical Biology, 2026)

facts.statement: Antusuchus is classified as a member of the family Peirosauridae.
facts.quote: A member of the family Peirosauridae.

facts.statement: Two individuals of Antusuchus were discovered in close proximity within the Cenomanian Candeleros Formation.
facts.quote: Antusuchus is known from two individuals that were found in close proximity of each other in the sediments of the Cenomanian Candeleros Formation

facts.statement: Fossils of Antusuchus date to the Albian stage.
Antusuchus fossils were found in the Rio Negro Province of Argentina, located in northern Patagonia.
facts.quote: The species name reflects the region the fossils were found in, the Rio Negro Province of Argentina, located in northern Patagonia.

facts.statement: Antusuchus had a small skull length of approximately 11.5 cm.
facts.quote: It has also been noted for its small size, with a skull length of 11.5 cm

facts.statement: Antusuchus was likely a carnivore, indicated by its blade-like and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: It's blade-like and serrated teeth indicate that it was a carnivore

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Antusuchus may have been a social animal living in groups, based on the discovery of two individuals found in close proximity.
facts.quote: The discovery of two Antusuchus individuals in close proximity may also suggest that like some uruguaysuchids, including Araripesuchus, Antusuchus may have been a social animal, possibly living in groups.

facts.statement: Antusuchus fossils come from the La Buitrera locality, an area interpreted as a wind-influenced dryland fluvian environment.
facts.quote: Antusuchus is specifically known from the La Buitrera locality of the La Buitrera Paleontological Area, which contains multipole sites that are interpreted to be wind-influenced dryland fluvian environments.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Antusuchus was the most basal member of the family Peirosauridae.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses conducted by Fernández-Dumont and colleagues consistently suggest that Antusuchus was the basalmost member of the family Peirosauridae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Antusuchus represents a distinct basal lineage or shows intermediate features between peirosaurids and other notosuchians.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis suggests that it may have been the most basal member of the family Peirosauridae. Despite this the animal shows a mix of features intermediate between peirosaurids and other notosuchians.

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen (MPCA PV 1294) includes an articulated skull and lower jaw, while a second specimen (MPCA PV 1295) consists of the middle to posterior parts of a skull.
rejected.quote: The holotype specimen, MPCA PV 1294, consists of an articulated skull and lower jaw while the second individual, MPCA PV 1295, is represented by the middle to posterior parts of a skull.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the middle to posterior parts of a skull'

rejected.statement: Antusuchus was described by Fernández-Dumont, Apesteguía, Pol, Bona, Pérez Mayoral, and Vega in 2026.
rejected.quote: Authors: María Lucila Fernández-Dumont, Sebastián Apesteguía, Diego Pol, Paula Bona, Joaquín Pérez Mayoral, Nahuel Vega
